classification.difficultyReason: Reuse the initial DB calculation with the midpoint relationship, construct NC, and compare the resulting vectors to prove collinearity.

content.prompt:
ABD is a triangle.

N is a point on AD such that $AN:ND=2:1$.

spec.description: Triangle ABD with AB extended to C, N on AD and M on BD. Directed labels establish AB=a, AN=2b and ND=b. The proposed line NMC is absent. Decorative grey triangle fill is omitted under the house diagram policy.
spec.mathematics: AN:ND=2:1; AB=BC; BM=MD. Arrows on AB, AN and ND point respectively A to B, A to N and N to D.
spec.answerVisibility: All directed givens remain visible; no solution line or vector calculation is supplied.

children.label: b
children.prompt:
B is the midpoint of AC.

M is the midpoint of BD.

Show that NMC is a straight line.

answer.short: $\overrightarrow{NM}=\frac12(-\underset{\sim}{b}+\underset{\sim}{a})$ and $\overrightarrow{NC}=2(-\underset{\sim}{b}+\underset{\sim}{a})=4\overrightarrow{NM}$. The vectors are parallel and share N, so N, M and C are collinear.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{NM}&=\overrightarrow{ND}+\overrightarrow{DM}\\\overrightarrow{NM}&=\underset{\sim}{b}+\frac12\overrightarrow{DB}\\\overrightarrow{NM}&=\underset{\sim}{b}+\frac12(-3\underset{\sim}{b}+\underset{\sim}{a})\\\overrightarrow{NM}&=\frac12(-\underset{\sim}{b}+\underset{\sim}{a})\\\overrightarrow{NC}&=\overrightarrow{NA}+\overrightarrow{AC}\\\overrightarrow{NC}&=-2\underset{\sim}{b}+2\underset{\sim}{a}\\\overrightarrow{NC}&=2(-\underset{\sim}{b}+\underset{\sim}{a})\\\overrightarrow{NC}&=4\overrightarrow{NM}\end{aligned}$$
The vectors $\overrightarrow{NM}$ and $\overrightarrow{NC}$ are parallel and share the common point N. Therefore N, M and C lie on a straight line.
